next_wave_cards.objective: Implement the aiworkhub_task_queue_request MCP tool in server.py per B281 section_1 queue_request_envelope schema. The tool accepts a queue_request JSON, validates it against the schema, checks idempotency (same request_id = no-op if still live), and returns the request status. No process launch -- the tool is a write-through to a new queue_requests JSONL append-only log at tools/aiworkhub/data/audit/mcp_queue_requests_b282_v1.jsonl.
acceptance: New tool aiworkhub_task_queue_request registered additively in server.py; existing tools unchanged (list_tools count check)
queue_request JSON validated against B281 section_1 schema; rejects malformed requests
Idempotency: same request_id submitted twice returns {status: 'duplicate', original_status: <current_state>}
Valid requests appended to mcp_queue_requests_b282_v1.jsonl with all envelope fields
request_id is deterministic sha1(task_id + runner + requested_at)[:16]
No process spawn; LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED remains false
Shell test validates schema, idempotency, and append behavior

next_wave_cards.objective: Implement a stale_recovery_orchestrator module that consumes build_completion_inbox()['stale_processing'] and produces a ranked recovery action list per B281 section_2 stale_recovery_flow. Actions: requeue (reset to pending with new runner), mark_done (superseded), kill_zombie (SIGTERM/SIGKILL if PID alive), or escalate_to_owner (unkillable zombie). No automatic execution of kill/requeue -- only detection and ranked recommendation.
acceptance: Module produces recovery_actions list from stale_processing facet input
Each action has: task_id, action_type (requeue|mark_done|kill_zombie|escalate), confidence, reason
Zombie detection: checks /proc/<pid> for recorded worker PIDs from launch log
Ranking: kill_zombie > requeue > mark_done > escalate (most recoverable first)
No automatic kill/requeue execution; all actions are recommendations only
Shell test with fixture stale_processing data covering all 4 action types

next_wave_cards.objective: Implement aiworkhub_task_cost_ledger MCP tool that UNIONs the 15-field launch log (B276 section_3) and aiworkhub_task_usage_report (existing tool) into a unified per-topic/per-runner/per-day cost view per B281 section_3 reconciliation_rules. Read-only: consumes two existing read paths, produces aggregates. No new write path.
acceptance: New tool aiworkhub_task_cost_ledger registered additively in server.py
UNION of launch_log + taskctl_usage with dedup by (task_id, runner, model)
Aggregates: total_cost_usd by topic, by runner, by day; per-task detail on request
Reconciliation rule: launch_log wins for gate events, taskctl_usage wins for final token counts
No write to any file; pure read-only aggregation
Shell test with fixture launch log + usage data

next_wave_cards.objective: Wire the full B281 queue flow into Codex's orchestration loop: auto_pickup -> queue_request creation (if CLAIMED and needs launch) -> completion_inbox delta polling -> review -> cost ledger recording. This is the FIRST task that actually connects the MCP queue tools into Codex's real orchestration cadence, replacing the manual 'copy command block to worker' flow.
acceptance: Codex loop: auto_pickup -> detect CLAIMED -> create queue_request -> poll completion_inbox -> review -> commit
Stale detection integrated: Codex checks stale_processing each loop iteration, triggers recovery actions
Cost ledger consulted before launching: if topic budget exceeded, skip launch and notify owner
DeepSeek manual adapter: Codex prints the command block for owner to copy (unchanged from current flow)
Dry-run mode (--dryrun) prints what WOULD be launched without creating queue_request

blockers: LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED_STILL_FALSE: G4 gate (B276 section_2) must be set to true before any process is actually spawned. This requires CODEX_TASK_MCP_AUTOLAUNCH_WIRE_PROCESS_B279_V1 to complete first.
OWNER_DELIVERY_CHANNEL_UNDECIDED: Per B277 blocker 1, no notification target exists for stale/failure/collision events that need owner attention.

DEEPSEEK_MANUAL_ADAPTER_IS_BY_DESIGN: DeepSeek runs as a separate chat session; the queue flow for deepseek_manual is always 'print command block for owner to copy' -- this is correct behavior, not a gap.

notes.b281_synthesis_value: B281 connects three previously separate specs (B276 autolaunch, B277 notification loop, B275 completion_inbox) into ONE coherent end-to-end queue flow. Before B281, each spec described its own piece; B281 defines how they compose: queue_request -> gate check -> launch -> completion_inbox detection -> stale recovery -> usage accounting -> cost ledger.
notes.state_machine_formalization: The 9-state/12-transition state machine in B281 section_4 is the first formal specification of the FULL task lifecycle across all MCP tools. Previously, lifecycle was implicit across taskctl states + completion_inbox facets + B276 launch states. B281 makes it explicit and testable.
notes.implementation_order: B282 (queue_request tool) -> B283 (stale recovery) + B284 (cost ledger) can run in parallel after B282. B278 (delta tool, B277 next_wave) is a prerequisite for B285 (Codex loop wiring). B279 (process spawn, B276 next_wave) is the final gate before any real launch.
